scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: Choose a useful record
scenes.caption: Kabir models the fictional applicant table. A stable ID, a practice score and document status support the exercise rules. Home addresses, bank details and photographs are unnecessary for the stated classroom task.
scenes.dialogue: What does this process actually need to know?

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: Names are not reliable keys
scenes.caption: Two separate applicants can have the same name, and one ID may appear twice. Overwriting a keyed record would hide that conflict. The model needs a stable identifier and a route for duplicate or missing data.
scenes.dialogue: A tidy table must not erase a conflict.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Pick the right representation
scenes.caption: A record holds one applicant’s fields. A list holds several records. A keyed lookup retrieves a unique record by its stable ID. A data dictionary states the meaning, type and validation rule for each field.
scenes.dialogue: Represent the task, not every detail about a person.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Protect the identifier
scenes.caption: Two supplied records contain the same applicant ID with conflicting values. Should a lookup silently keep the newest row, or should the conflict be flagged for review before a unique record is used?
scenes.dialogue: Do not hide disagreement by overwriting it.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: A minimal model
scenes.caption: Kabir defines an ID as an uppercase letter and two digits. Scores must be finite values from zero to one hundred; missing data stays missing. Document status distinguishes complete, incomplete and unknown. Duplicate IDs remain visible.
scenes.dialogue: The field meaning is part of the model.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the logic lab
scenes.caption: Select necessary fields, match records, lists and keyed lookups to their jobs, and inspect validation routes. Use synthetic records only. A clear model makes the later algorithm’s inputs and limits easier to explain.
scenes.dialogue: Let us make the data rules explicit too.
